jobs:
  # B8 (2026-09-12) — a run that cannot get its runner fails by name. The
  # only runner carrying [self-hosted, linux, claude] went offline on
  # 2026-09-08 09:48Z; every scheduled run since queued with zero jobs and
  # was CANCELLED ~12h later by the next schedule taking this concurrency
  # group's single pending slot (cancel-in-progress: false keeps ONE pending
  # run). No red, no error, no notification: green by absence. This hosted
  # job refuses the run with a named reason unless an ONLINE runner carries
  # every label the self-hosted job needs; the self-hosted job `needs` it,
  # so a run is either dispatched or red within a minute. One definition
  # for every self-hosted lane: .github/actions/require-self-hosted-runner
  # (decision logic: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/runner_availability.py; wiring
  # pinned by aria-kernel/tests/test_runner_availability.py).
  runner-preflight:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: ./.github/actions/require-self-hosted-runner
        with:
          # Verbatim the self-hosted job's runs-on; the invariant test
          # compares the two so they cannot drift apart.
          required-labels: self-hosted,linux,claude
          app-id: ${{ secrets.ARIA_GH_APP_ID }}
          app-installation-id: ${{ secrets.ARIA_GH_APP_INSTALLATION_ID }}
          app-private-key: ${{ secrets.ARIA_GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

  cycle:
    needs: runner-preflight
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, claude]
    # Mode-aware sizing: a REAL observe burn-in is 30 kernel-guarded cycles at
    # ~2.5 min/cycle ≈ 80-90 min (run 28577469404 was cancelled mid-burn-in by
    # the previous flat 50-minute limit, producing ZERO ladder evidence because
    # the acceptance verdict is all-or-nothing). Schedule/cycle runs keep 50.
    # Operator decision (2026-08-13): the night's window is UNBOUNDED — in
    # GitHub terms that is the 360-minute platform ceiling, stated
    # explicitly rather than left implicit by omitting the field. Smoke
    # runs 1-3 proved the 50-minute cap was the binding constraint (the
    # cycle needs adapters + queue drain + spawns); the deadline defence
    # pair (ORPHAN-661 spawn clamp + ORPHAN-662 night-close) keeps ANY
    # value safe: the night seals and publishes whatever the wall is.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    env:
      # Kernel-workflow parity: no .pyc litter in the checkout — the
      # burn-in pre-clean guard treats any untracked path as dirty.
      PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: '1'
    steps:
      # ORPHAN-HIGH-802 — reset the persistent workspace HERE, so checkout
      # does not have to. actions/checkout's `clean` runs `git clean -ffdx`,
      # and `-x` deletes gitignored paths — including node_modules, which the
      # worktree-clean guard this cleaning exists to satisfy never inspects,
      # because `git status` does not report ignored files. The cost was paid
      # every run: a full `npm ci` (measured 2m50s, ~1.6 GB peak RSS) on a
      # self-hosted runner that shares its box with production and is
      # deliberately the first OOM victim (oom_score_adj=500). The kernel
      # killed that install on 2026-09-03 and twice more, and each kill left
      # node_modules half-populated, so the NEXT run reinstalled from scratch
      # and was killed again. Same reset, one exclusion, loop gone.
      - name: Reset the persistent workspace, keeping installed dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -d .git ]; then
            git reset --hard
            git clean -ffdx -e node_modules
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

# (02:00 UTC) only drains an already-minted queue; this workflow runs the
# full `aria-kernel autonomy run` orchestration (discovery → pressure →
# triage → planner/bridge/worker drains) nightly.
#
# ORPHAN-HIGH-728 — the profile is RESOLVED, not fixed, and the resolution
# is BOUNDED. The `profile_gate` step calls
# `autonomy_unlock.resolve_scheduled_profile`, which proposes `strict` when
# the L1 ladder is valid and then bounds that proposal by the
# operator-recorded `scheduler_profile_ceiling` (default `standard`). Strict
# is what `runtime_profile` defines as the full implementation pipeline
# (claim → planned → committed → validated → PR); standard withholds
# `pr_create`, which is why this lane used to converge plans it could never
# turn into a pull request — and why reaching strict on a schedule takes an
# operator gesture rather than a night of good evidence. Merge authority is
# untouched by either: `pr_merge` is autonomous-only and no resolution here
# can emit `autonomous`.
#
# Two dispatch modes:
#   mode=cycle           — one ceiling-bounded, L1-resolved cycle (default)
#   mode=burn-in-observe — REAL-mode observe burn-in (30 cycles, LLM-free)
#                          + the operator bridge that records
#                          observe_success acceptance events toward the
#                          L1 autonomy unlock (Plan 031c ladder).
#
# State model (PLAN Wave 1 PR 2.6b — the lane cutover): ARIA's whole
# runtime state travels between runs on the `aria/state` branch — checkout
# the tip, run against it, fast-forward-push. The enterprise
# acceptance/unlock ledgers and monthly cost-attribution shards must
# accumulate between nights, and the 30-day artifact that used to carry
# them could not enforce that: `overwrite: true` would bury the
# accumulated tree under a bootstrap-empty one, and an empty tree passes
# `integrity verify` because it is trivially consistent.
#
# There is NO fail-open on state any more. A restore that cannot reach a
# published tip fails the run; it does not start over quietly. Fresh
# bootstrap now requires `vars.ARIA_STATE_BOOTSTRAP_ACK` — an operator
# naming the repository — because a process that can create the branch
# when it cannot SEE it is a process that replaces history with emptiness
# on a network blip. Auth/policy stay fail-closed as before.
#
# Brakes (all pre-existing kernel mechanisms):
#   - vars.ARIA_MOCK_KILL_SWITCH (read AHEAD of dispatch input/default)
#   - ARIA_STOP file in the store's tools root → orchestrator exits cleanly
#   - cross-host autonomous-loop lease (refuses when a local daemon runs)
#   - per-cycle wall-clock deadline (--cycle-deadline-seconds) + the
#     executor's pre-dispatch wall-clock ceiling derived from this job's
#     own timeout-minutes. ORPHAN-HIGH-472 removed the USD caps that used
#     to be listed here: ARIA runs on a Claude Code subscription session,
#     so there is no per-run charge for a dollar cap to bound, and the two
#     figures ($20.00/run, $3.00/cycle) contradicted each other anyway.
#   - concurrency group, cancel-in-progress: false

on:
  schedule:
    # 17:13 UTC = 19:13 Oslo (CEST) — operator decision 2026-08-27: the cycle
    # runs INSIDE the operator's evening work window (7pm Norway), not at
    # night, so the operator can watch the run and intervene while awake.
    # Still before aria-agent-executor's drain so queue rows this cycle
    # leaves behind get a second drain pass the same evening.
    # 13 past, not :00 — GitHub fires top-of-hour crons up to ~75min late
    # under shared-infra load (measured 2026-08-18: 01:00 fired 02:13).
    - cron: '13 17 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      mode:
        description: 'cycle = one cycle at min(operator scheduler ceiling, L1 ladder verdict); burn-in-observe = REAL observe burn-in + L1 ladder bridge'
        required: false
        default: 'cycle'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'cycle'
          - 'burn-in-observe'

        description: 'Cycles per invocation (mode=cycle only)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
        type: string
      unquarantine_tool_ids:
        description: 'Comma-separated tool ids to unquarantine before the cycle (audited; one approval ref per id)'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string

        description: 'Comma-separated gh:<owner>/<repo>#<n>/comment/<id> (or /review/<id>) refs, one per tool id in order: operator GitHub acts carrying `aria-kernel operator approval-template --surface tool_unquarantine tool=<id>`'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      mock:
        description: 'Run in mock mode (no real Claude Code CLI invocation)'
        required: false
        default: 'false'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'true'
          - 'false'

# turn into a pull request — and why reaching strict on a schedule takes an

# runtime state travels between runs on the `aria/state` branch — checkout
# the tip, run against it, fast-forward-push. The enterprise
# acceptance/unlock ledgers and monthly cost-attribution shards must
# accumulate between nights, and the 30-day artifact that used to carry
# them could not enforce that: `overwrite: true` would bury the
# accumulated tree under a bootstrap-empty one, and an empty tree passes
# `integrity verify` because it is trivially consistent.

## TenantConfigurationPage — `/admin/tenants/:tenantId/configuration` — verdict: **MOCK_ONLY**

**Chain:** Routing and auth verified working: FE tenantConfigApi
(web/modules/admin-panel/src/services/api/tenant-config.ts) hits '/api/settings/tenant/:tenantId/_',
nginx rewrites ^/api/(._) to /api/v1/$1 (infrastructure/nginx/droplet.conf:382), matching
admin-api's global prefix 'api/v1' (libs/backend-common/src/bootstrap/create-service-app.ts:610) +
TenantConfigurationController @Controller('settings/tenant')
(apps/admin-api-service/src/settings/controllers/tenant-configuration.controller.ts:42); all
requests pass the global PlatformAdminGuard (RS256 JWT + SUPER_ADMIN,
apps/admin-api-service/src/app.module.ts:283-290, guards/platform-admin.guard.ts:59,155-177). But
the persistence layer does not exist: TenantConfigurationService is an explicit 'legacy adapter' —
every GET synthesizes the same hardcoded createDefaultTenantConfiguration() object for every tenant
(tenant-configuration.service.ts:349-358, entities/tenant-configuration.entity.ts:277-389) and every
mutation (all 9 tab saves, API keys, webhooks, domain verification, IP lists, module toggles) throws
GoneException 410 (tenant-configuration.service.ts:360-362). The backing table
admin.tenant_configurations was dropped by migration 1801400000000 (rows archived to
admin.retired_config_backups); the promised config-service replacement was never wired for tenant
scope — usePlatformConfiguration.ts only covers the 'platform' service namespace. The page is fully
rendered, routed (Module.tsx:114) and looks functional, but is 100% decorative.

**Endpoints exercised:** `GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/user-limits`;
`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/storage`;

`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/branding`;
`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/security, POST/DELETE .../security/ip-whitelist(/:ip), POST/DELETE .../security/ip-blacklist(/:ip)`;
`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/notifications`;
`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/features, POST .../features/modules/:moduleCode/enable|disable`;
`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/data-retention`;
`POST /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/webhooks/:webhookId/test (FE only — no backend route)`

`admin.tenant_configurations — DROPPED by migration 1801400000000-DropRetiredLegacyConfigStores.ts (no live table backs this page)`,

### APA-033 [HIGH] Every mutation on the page returns 410 Gone — no tenant configuration can be changed at all

- **Status:** CONFIRMED+DESIGNED (audited CRITICAL → verified HIGH)
- **Symptom:** All write endpoints route into TenantConfigurationService.throwLegacyGone(): the Save
  buttons on all 9 tabs (user limits, storage, API, branding, security, notifications, feature
  flags, data retention), API-key create/revoke, webhook create/update/delete, domain verification
  initiate/confirm, IP whitelist/blacklist add/remove, and module enable/disable ALL throw
  GoneException ('admin-api direct tenant_configurations writes are retired; use config-service
  effective configuration APIs'). The FE catches these and shows generic 'Failed to save X.'
  banners, so the operator gets no hint that the feature is permanently retired rather than
  transiently failing. The entire admin surface for per-tenant configuration is a dead end.
- **Evidence:**
  - `apps/admin-api-service/src/settings/services/tenant-configuration.service.ts:94-95`
  - `apps/admin-api-service/src/settings/services/tenant-configuration.service.ts:148-154`

  - `web/modules/admin-panel/src/pages/TenantConfigurationPage.tsx:272-285`
  - `web/modules/admin-panel/src/pages/TenantConfigurationPage.tsx:572-583`
- **Verification:** Prior adversarial verification confirmed the chain end-to-end; re-reading
  confirms it and reveals the full retirement context. Every write method in
  apps/admin-api-service/src/settings/services/tenant-configuration.service.ts is typed `: never`
  and terminates in throwLegacyGone() (GoneException 410); tenant-configuration.controller.ts wires
  all PUT/POST/DELETE on settings/tenant/\* to them. The backing table admin.tenant_configurations
  was archived into admin.retired_config_backups and DROPPED by migration
  1801400000000-DropRetiredLegacyConfigStores.ts (ORPHAN-HIGH-364) — forward-only, down() is a
  deliberate no-op. The named successor ('config-service effective configuration APIs') is a generic
  tenant/service/key/environment KV exposed only as a federated GraphQL subgraph
  (configuration.resolver.ts: effectiveConfiguration, effectiveConfigurationsByService,
  setConfiguration); it has no structured tenant-configuration model and no API-key minting, webhook
  registry, or domain-verification capability. Severity stays HIGH (not CRITICAL): total loss of an
  admin capability plus fabricated GET data (defaultConfiguration() with epoch timestamps)
  misleading operators, but no data corruption or security breach — writes fail closed.
- **Root cause:** The chain was severed intentionally at the BE service layer as the backend half of
  a config-store retirement that was never finished. The DB-audit remediation (ORPHAN-HIGH-364)
  retired the 'legacy trio' (admin.global_configs, admin.system_settings,
  admin.tenant_configurations) to config-service: writes were 410'd, entities undecorated, tables
  archived+dropped. But the migration stopped at the service boundary — neither the successor
  capability (structured tenant-config sections in config-service; today it is a bare KV with no
  section vocabulary, and no replacement exists for the behavioral resources: API-key minting,
  webhooks, domain verification) nor the consumer (TenantConfigurationPage + tenantConfigApi, still
  pointed at the retired routes) was migrated. The drift stayed invisible for 'multiple releases'
  (the migration's own words) because of two structural gaps: (1) the FE api layer is a hand-written
  mirror of retired backend interfaces (tenant-config.ts literally says 'mirror backend entity
  interfaces') with no build- or test-time contract binding FE route usage to live BE routes — a
  route that throws 410-by-design is indistinguishable from a live one to the FE build; and (2) the
  GET endpoints synthesize plausible per-tenant defaults instead of failing, so the page renders
  convincingly and only breaks on Save, where the FE catch blocks discard error detail into generic
  'Failed to save X.' banners.
- **Fix design:** Systemic class: half-retired legacy surface (BE 410'd, FE untouched, successor
  unbuilt) — the identical pattern exists in system-setting.service.ts:419. Fix at pattern level

### APA-033 [HIGH] Every mutation on the page returns 410 Gone — no tenant configuration can be changed at all

- **Status:** CONFIRMED+DESIGNED (audited CRITICAL → verified HIGH)
- **Symptom:** All write endpoints route into TenantConfigurationService.throwLegacyGone(): the Save
  buttons on all 9 tabs (user limits, storage, API, branding, security, notifications, feature
  flags, data retention), API-key create/revoke, webhook create/update/delete, domain verification
  initiate/confirm, IP whitelist/blacklist add/remove, and module enable/disable ALL throw
  GoneException ('admin-api direct tenant_configurations writes are retired; use config-service
  effective configuration APIs'). The FE catches these and shows generic 'Failed to save X.'
  banners, so the operator gets no hint that the feature is permanently retired rather than
  transiently failing. The entire admin surface for per-tenant configuration is a dead end.

### APA-033 [HIGH] Every mutation on the page returns 410 Gone — no tenant configuration can be changed at all

- **Status:** CONFIRMED+DESIGNED (audited CRITICAL → verified HIGH)
- **Symptom:** All write endpoints route into TenantConfigurationService.throwLegacyGone(): the Save
  buttons on all 9 tabs (user limits, storage, API, branding, security, notifications, feature
  flags, data retention), API-key create/revoke, webhook create/update/delete, domain verification
  initiate/confirm, IP whitelist/blacklist add/remove, and module enable/disable ALL throw
  GoneException ('admin-api direct tenant_configurations writes are retired; use config-service
  effective configuration APIs'). The FE catches these and shows generic 'Failed to save X.'
  banners, so the operator gets no hint that the feature is permanently retired rather than
  transiently failing. The entire admin surface for per-tenant configuration is a dead end.
- **Evidence:**
  - `apps/admin-api-service/src/settings/services/tenant-configuration.service.ts:94-95`
  - `apps/admin-api-service/src/settings/services/tenant-configuration.service.ts:148-154`
  - `apps/admin-api-service/src/settings/services/tenant-configuration.service.ts:208-222`

  - `apps/admin-api-service/src/settings/services/tenant-configuration.service.ts:303-309`
  - `apps/admin-api-service/src/settings/services/tenant-configuration.service.ts:360-362`
  - `web/modules/admin-panel/src/pages/TenantConfigurationPage.tsx:272-285`
  - `web/modules/admin-panel/src/pages/TenantConfigurationPage.tsx:572-583`
- **Verification:** Prior adversarial verification confirmed the chain end-to-end; re-reading
  confirms it and reveals the full retirement context. Every write method in
  apps/admin-api-service/src/settings/services/tenant-configuration.service.ts is typed `: never`
  and terminates in throwLegacyGone() (GoneException 410); tenant-configuration.controller.ts wires
  all PUT/POST/DELETE on settings/tenant/\* to them. The backing table admin.tenant_configurations
  was archived into admin.retired_config_backups and DROPPED by migration
  1801400000000-DropRetiredLegacyConfigStores.ts (ORPHAN-HIGH-364) — forward-only, down() is a
  deliberate no-op. The named successor ('config-service effective configuration APIs') is a generic
  tenant/service/key/environment KV exposed only as a federated GraphQL subgraph
  (configuration.resolver.ts: effectiveConfiguration, effectiveConfigurationsByService,
  setConfiguration); it has no structured tenant-configuration model and no API-key minting, webhook
  registry, or domain-verification capability. Severity stays HIGH (not CRITICAL): total loss of an
  admin capability plus fabricated GET data (defaultConfiguration() with epoch timestamps)
  misleading operators, but no data corruption or security breach — writes fail closed.
- **Root cause:** The chain was severed intentionally at the BE service layer as the backend half of
  a config-store retirement that was never finished. The DB-audit remediation (ORPHAN-HIGH-364)
  retired the 'legacy trio' (admin.global_configs, admin.system_settings,
  admin.tenant_configurations) to config-service: writes were 410'd, entities undecorated, tables
  archived+dropped. But the migration stopped at the service boundary — neither the successor
  capability (structured tenant-config sections in config-service; today it is a bare KV with no
  section vocabulary, and no replacement exists for the behavioral resources: API-key minting,
  webhooks, domain verification) nor the consumer (TenantConfigurationPage + tenantConfigApi, still
  pointed at the retired routes) was migrated. The drift stayed invisible for 'multiple releases'
  (the migration's own words) because of two structural gaps: (1) the FE api layer is a hand-written
  mirror of retired backend interfaces (tenant-config.ts literally says 'mirror backend entity
  interfaces') with no build- or test-time contract binding FE route usage to live BE routes — a
  route that throws 410-by-design is indistinguishable from a live one to the FE build; and (2) the
  GET endpoints synthesize plausible per-tenant defaults instead of failing, so the page renders
  convincingly and only breaks on Save, where the FE catch blocks discard error detail into generic
  'Failed to save X.' banners.
- **Fix design:** Systemic class: half-retired legacy surface (BE 410'd, FE untouched, successor
  unbuilt) — the identical pattern exists in system-setting.service.ts:419. Fix at pattern level
  plus local application, completing the retirement in the direction the decision-of-record chose

**Chain:** Routing and auth verified working: FE tenantConfigApi

nginx rewrites ^/api/(._) to /api/v1/$1 (infrastructure/nginx/droplet.conf:382), matching
admin-api's global prefix 'api/v1' (libs/backend-common/src/bootstrap/create-service-app.ts:610) +
TenantConfigurationController @Controller('settings/tenant')

requests pass the global PlatformAdminGuard (RS256 JWT + SUPER_ADMIN,

the persistence layer does not exist: TenantConfigurationService is an explicit 'legacy adapter' —

admin.tenant_configurations was dropped by migration 1801400000000 (rows archived to
admin.retired_config_backups); the promised config-service replacement was never wired for tenant
scope — usePlatformConfiguration.ts only covers the 'platform' service namespace. The page is fully
rendered, routed (Module.tsx:114) and looks functional, but is 100% decorative.

`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/notifications`;
`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/features, POST .../features/modules/:moduleCode/enable|disable`;
`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/data-retention`;
`POST /api/v1/settings/tenant/:tenantId/webhooks/:webhookId/test (FE only — no backend route)`

### APA-033 [HIGH] Every mutation on the page returns 410 Gone — no tenant configuration can be changed at all

- **Status:** CONFIRMED+DESIGNED (audited CRITICAL → verified HIGH)
- **Symptom:** All write endpoints route into TenantConfigurationService.throwLegacyGone(): the Save
  buttons on all 9 tabs (user limits, storage, API, branding, security, notifications, feature
  flags, data retention), API-key create/revoke, webhook create/update/delete, domain verification
  initiate/confirm, IP whitelist/blacklist add/remove, and module enable/disable ALL throw
  GoneException ('admin-api direct tenant_configurations writes are retired; use config-service
  effective configuration APIs'). The FE catches these and shows generic 'Failed to save X.'
  banners, so the operator gets no hint that the feature is permanently retired rather than
